title.en: Follow the structure of a talk
title.es: Seguir la estructura de una charla

es: Seguir la estructura de una charla en audio (apertura, puntos principales, desvíos y cierre), anotar sus puntos clave a partir de las señales del orador e inferir su postura.

teaching.en: The keynote speaker said she would cover three main points: cost, safety and comfort, and that she would spell out the key figures for each one.
teaching.es: La ponente principal dijo que abordaría tres puntos principales: el costo, la seguridad y la comodidad, y que explicaría con detalle las cifras clave de cada uno.
teaching.explanationEs: Cover + main points anuncia el esquema; spell out = explicar sin dar nada por sabido; anota cuántos puntos son.
segments: The keynote speaker said she would cover three main points: cost, safety and
comfort, and that she would spell out the key figures for each one.
teaching.audioText: The keynote speaker said she would cover three main points: cost, safety and comfort, and that she would spell out the key figures for each one.

teaching.en: After a short preamble about the school, the first key point was cost: a monthly ticket now costs forty euros, the main obstacle for students.
teaching.es: Tras un breve preámbulo sobre el colegio, el primer punto clave fue el costo: un pasaje mensual cuesta ahora cuarenta euros, el principal obstáculo para los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: The first key point is… abre el punto 1; el preámbulo no cuenta como punto; después viene el dato que conviene anotar.
segments: After a short preamble about the school, the first key point was cost:
a monthly ticket now costs forty euros, the main obstacle for students.
teaching.audioText: After a short preamble about the school, the first key point was cost: a monthly ticket now costs forty euros, the main obstacle for students.

teaching.en: Briefly, the second point was safety, and she went off on a tangent about street lighting, so some listeners began to lose track of the structure of the talk.
teaching.es: En pocas palabras, el segundo punto fue la seguridad, y se fue por la tangente con el alumbrado de las calles, así que algunos oyentes empezaron a perder el hilo de la estructura de la charla.
teaching.explanationEs: Briefly avisa de que el punto será corto; go off on a tangent = desviarse; lose track = perder el hilo.
segments: Briefly, the second point was safety, and she went off on a tangent about street
lighting, so some listeners began to lose track of the structure of the talk.
teaching.audioText: Briefly, the second point was safety, and she went off on a tangent about street lighting, so some listeners began to lose track of the structure of the talk.

teaching.en: To recap, she will wrap up by repeating the three points, so the audience can home in on one clear takeaway.
teaching.es: Para recapitular, cerrará repitiendo los tres puntos, de modo que el público pueda centrarse en una idea clara.
teaching.explanationEs: To recap señala el cierre; wrap up = concluir; home in on = centrarse en lo esencial, el mensaje que debe quedarte.
segments: To recap, she will wrap up by repeating the three points,
so the audience can home in on one clear takeaway.
teaching.audioText: To recap, she will wrap up by repeating the three points, so the audience can home in on one clear takeaway.

teaching.en: While I listen, I note down each key word, not full sentences, and when a speaker chooses to elaborate on a point, I add only one detail.
teaching.es: Mientras escucho, anoto cada palabra clave, no frases completas, y cuando un orador decide ampliar un punto, añado solo un detalle.
teaching.explanationEs: Note down + palabras clave; elaborate on = ampliar un punto con más detalle, que tú resumes en un solo dato.
segments: While I listen, I note down each key word, not full sentences, and when
a speaker chooses to elaborate on a point, I add only one detail.
teaching.audioText: While I listen, I note down each key word, not full sentences, and when a speaker chooses to elaborate on a point, I add only one detail.

teaching.en: A good listener notices when a speaker goes off on a tangent and waits for the signal that the main line has resumed.
teaching.es: Un buen oyente se da cuenta de cuándo el orador se va por la tangente y espera la señal de que se retoma la línea principal.
teaching.explanationEs: No todo lo que se dice es un punto del esquema: un desvío no se anota como punto principal.
segments: A good listener notices when a speaker goes off on a tangent
and waits for the signal that the main line has resumed.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué trata la charla y cómo se organiza.

choices.text: The library's opening hours, explained in detail.
The school library, divided into three points.
A plan to build a new library within three years.

feedback.es: La oradora anuncia que abordará tres puntos principales sobre la biblioteca del colegio; el horario es solo uno de ellos.

hint.es: Escucha la señal de apertura: dice el tema y cuántos puntos anuncia.

origin.audio: Hello, everyone. Today I will cover three main points about our school library: opening hours, books and study spaces, and I will spell out what each one would cost.

prompt.es: Completa: «El primer punto clave es el horario.»

feedback.es: The first key point is… abre el primer punto; key (o main) lo marca como una idea importante que conviene anotar.

origin.text: The speaker announced three main points. She said the first ___ point was opening hours, because the library closes at four.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para recapitular, el orador repitió sus tres puntos clave.»

answer.text: To recap the speaker repeated her three key points

feedback.es: To recap va al principio y señala el cierre; después viene lo que se resume.

hint.es: Empieza con To recap y termina con los puntos clave.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ventaja económica señala el orador.

choices.text: A bus pass is cheaper than a bike for most families.
A bike saves money only for students who live nearby.
A bike costs less than a bus pass after about ten months.

feedback.es: El primer punto clave es el costo: tras unos diez meses, la bicicleta resulta más barata que el pase mensual de autobús.

origin.audio: Good morning, everyone. Today I will cover three main points about cycling to school: cost, safety and comfort. The first key point is cost. A bike becomes cheaper than a monthly bus pass after about ten months, and that matters to many families. Briefly, the second point is safety: since the new lane opened, accidents near the school have fallen by a third. Finally, comfort. I will spell out why students arrive calmer and more awake. To recap, cycling is cheaper, safer and healthier.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del orador con la señal que da al oyente.

pairs: The first key point is cost.
Briefly, the second point is safety.

pairs.es: avisa de que el punto será corto

pairs: But that is a tangent, so back to the structure.

pairs.es: vuelve al hilo tras un desvío

pairs: To recap, the talk has three parts.

feedback.es: Cada señal dice dónde está el oyente: abre un punto, anuncia brevedad, marca el regreso de un desvío o abre el cierre.

pairs: The first key point is cost.

pairs.es: avisa de que el punto será corto

pairs: But that is a tangent, so back to the structure.

pairs.es: vuelve al hilo tras un desvío

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dato conviene anotar para el punto del espacio de estudio.

choices.text: Twelve desks for eight hundred students.
Eight hundred students working in pairs.
Twelve students for every desk in the room.

feedback.es: El dato clave es la proporción: solo doce mesas para ochocientos estudiantes; el resto es detalle para no anotar.

origin.audio: The second key point is study space. There are only twelve desks for eight hundred students, which means that most of them have to work on the floor or in the corridor.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué anuncia el orador para el final de la charla.

choices.text: A list of the dishes removed from the menu.
An explanation of why the early increase matters.
A survey of complaints from students.

feedback.es: El orador promete volver en el cierre sobre por qué importa que el aumento se concentre en el primer mes; las otras opciones son detalles del desarrollo.

origin.audio: Thank you for coming. My talk has two parts: first, how the canteen changed its menu, and then whether students actually eat more vegetables. The short answer is yes, but only slightly. Salad sales rose by about ten percent, although most of that increase came in the first month, and I will come back to why that matters in my closing. In September, the canteen removed sweet drinks on Mondays and Fridays, and complaints were few.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué opina el orador del efecto del nuevo menú.

choices.text: It has failed, because students dislike vegetables.
It has completely changed what students eat at lunch.
It has helped, but less than one might expect.

feedback.es: «Yes, but only slightly» y un aumento concentrado en el primer mes indican un efecto real pero modesto.

origin.audio: Thank you for coming. My talk has two parts: first, how the canteen changed its menu, and then whether students actually eat more vegetables. The short answer is yes, but only slightly. Salad sales rose by about ten percent, although most of that increase came in the first month, and I will come back to why that matters in my closing. In September, the canteen removed sweet drinks on Mondays and Fridays, and complaints were few.

prompt.es: Completa: «Después de la charla, debes poder decir la idea clave en una frase.»

feedback.es: El takeaway es la idea que debe quedarte tras la charla, más allá de los detalles y los datos sueltos.

origin.text: A talk can contain many details. After it ends, the listener should be able to state the main ___ in one sentence.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El orador cerró con un resumen de sus tres puntos.»

answer.text: The speaker wrapped up with a summary of his three points

feedback.es: Wrapped up with + resumen expresa que el orador concluyó la charla con una síntesis de lo dicho.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función tiene la primera frase de este fragmento de la charla?

choices.text: It opens a short side story before the talk continues.
It introduces the closing summary of the talk.
It announces the second of the three main points.

feedback.es: «A small tangent» avisa de un desvío breve y «anyway, back to…» marca el regreso: la anécdota no es un punto del esquema.

origin.text: Before I go on, a small tangent: my grandfather used to cycle to school in all weathers, and he never once complained. Anyway, back to the second key point, which is safety.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la oradora sobre el tercer punto.

choices.text: It is the most urgent and should be done first.
It looks minor, yet the other two depend on it.
It can wait until the other two are solved.

feedback.es: Admite que el tercer punto parece menos urgente, pero sostiene que sin salas tranquilas los otros dos servirán de poco.

origin.audio: To recap, the library needs longer hours, more desks and quieter rooms. I know the third point may sound less urgent than the other two, but without a quiet place to study, extra hours and extra desks will not help much.

prompt.es: Completa: «Explicó cada cifra con detalle y definió cada palabra difícil.»

feedback.es: Spell out significa explicar algo con todo detalle, sin dar nada por sabido; encaja con un público muy variado.

origin.text: The audience came from many backgrounds, so the speaker did not assume anything. She was careful to ___ out every figure and to explain each difficult word.
